newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-DENILSON REPORTED NEAR TO JOINING BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DENILSON REPORTED NEAR TO JOINING BARCELONA.

text.p: Sao Paulo's 19-year-old midfielder Denilson is on the verge of a monster transfer to Spanish giants Barcelona, news reports said Saturday.

Brazilian newspapers and television stations said terms had been agreed between the two clubs and that the player would be travelling to Spain over the weekend to finalise a deal that could become a world record-breaker.
Barcelona were prepared to pay between $22 million and $24 million for the hugely talented player, reports claimed.

But Sao Paulo would also receive Barcelona's unsettled Brazilian international Giovanni, who despite erratic form since joining the Spanish club a year ago is still valued at between $10 million and $12 million, reports said.
In addition, Denilson himself could pocket a signing fee of up to $5 million, according to the Gazeta Esportiva sports daily.

This could bring the total value of the deal to around $40 million, a new record in the ever-spiralling international transfer market. Nobody was available at Sao Paulo to confirm reports of the deal.

Gazeta Esportivo quoted Denilson's agent as saying: "Everything is agreed between the clubs, all we need now is the agreement between Denilson and Barcelona. There's nothing Denilson, whose full name is Denilson de Oliveira but who like many Brazilian players is popularly known simply by his first name, was raised at Sao Paulo and made his first team debut at the age of 17.
He caught international attention with his performances in the Tournoi de France and the Copa America in June, where his runs down the left wing caused opposing defences constant problems.
He has won 10 full caps and was in the team that won the Copa America final against Bolivia.
During the competition, Brazil coach Mario Zagallo heaped praised on the player and said he had the characteristics of an old-fashioned winger.
